stem.en: Which set of parts must all work together for you to lift a school bag off the floor?

text.en: Bones, muscles, tendons, joints and nervous tissue, all working together.

feedback.en: Yes. Nervous tissue signals the muscle, the muscle contracts, the tendon passes the pull to the bone, and the bone moves at a joint.

text.en: Muscles alone, because only muscles contract and produce a pull.

feedback.en: No. A muscle that contracts with no tendon and no bone only bunches up. The pull must reach a bone that can move at a joint.

text.en: Bones and joints alone, because a firm frame that can bend is enough to make a movement.

feedback.en: No. Joints allow movement, but they cannot move the bones on their own. Muscles must pull on the bones.

text.en: Muscles, tendons, bones and joints, but not nervous tissue, since muscles contract whenever they need to.

feedback.en: No. Muscles cannot work on their own. They receive their instructions from nervous tissue.

hints.en: Which tissue tells a muscle when to contract?
Can a joint move a bone by itself?

explanation.en: Lifting a bag needs every link in the chain. Nervous tissue sends the instruction, the muscle contracts, the tendon passes the pull to the bone, and the bone moves at a joint. Remove any one of these, and the bag stays on the floor.
